bad_pattern: Code/file exists, so report PASS without executing required evidence.
why_wrong: Presence is only E0; runtime/integration/deployment claims require matching evidence class.
correct_response: Use NOT_VERIFIED until required evidence executes successfully.

bad_pattern: Reuse a green DOC-E/test artifact from an older commit as proof for current HEAD.
When canonical backend/system state cannot be fetched, silently assume READY/success.
why_wrong: Presentation turns uncertainty into false truth and may enable unsafe actions.
correct_response: Expose UNKNOWN/error/frozen-safe behavior and fail closed.

bad_pattern: Implement a permissive superset FSM with extra transitions/events because it seems more flexible.
why_wrong: It creates behavior outside DOC-C authority and can bypass legal sequencing.
correct_response: Use exact authorized event/transition set; spec extension/version bump for new semantics.

bad_pattern: Let UI, SWARM, external model, or lower-authority prose override CORE/LAW/current build authority.
why_wrong: NEXY separates labor/presentation from truth authority.
correct_response: Route through current authority graph and release gates.

bad_pattern: While fixing Queue, also redesign unrelated AUTH/UI/future architecture because it appears cleaner.
why_wrong: Adjacent usefulness is not authorization and expands regression surface.
correct_response: Repair the smallest complete root cause within authorized dependency impact.

bad_pattern: Keep success/pending UI visible or actionable while backend authoritative state is FREEZE.
why_wrong: UI truth layer must not mask or invent state.
correct_response: Display FREEZE, incident, and legal recovery/action availability.

bad_pattern: Deploy because build passes locally or evidence documents are present.
why_wrong: DOC-E requires exact executed evidence and external signoff; implementation-ready != deployable.
correct_response: Keep NON_DEPLOYABLE until all mandatory gates are current and pass.

bad_pattern: Allow unordered parallel workers/system time/RNG to mutate canonical Core state directly.
why_wrong: Constitutional deterministic law requires one canonical mutator and explicit ordered inputs.
correct_response: Keep nondeterministic workers non-authoritative and serialize canonical mutation.

bad_pattern: Change tests/thresholds to match current implementation when implementation conflicts with authoritative spec.
why_wrong: Tests cease to prove the requirement and encode drift as success.
correct_response: Re-read authority; fix implementation or explicitly change/version spec through legal path.

bad_pattern: Treat rollback SQL/script existence as proof rollback works.
why_wrong: Migration recovery is an execution claim.
correct_response: Run apply→rollback against real target-like DB and verify schema/state restoration.

bad_pattern: Store incident ID somewhere in payload and assume incident graph integrity is enforced.
why_wrong: Orphan/mismatch states remain possible without first-class contract/persistence enforcement.
correct_response: Enforce incident linkage in schema/storage/runtime and test orphan rejection.

bad_pattern: Producer/consumer queue schemas disagree, so invent a mapping that seems reasonable.
why_wrong: Missing authority is not permission to define semantics.
correct_response: BLOCK/FREEZE implementation until governing contract is explicit.

bad_pattern: Pick an arbitrary numeric coverage threshold because CI does not enforce one.
why_wrong: A generated number becomes fake authority.
correct_response: Record coverage gate gap and keep exact threshold UNKNOWN/BLOCKED until authorized.

bad_pattern: AI writes its own release signoff to satisfy E11.
why_wrong: Independent external authorization cannot be self-issued by the implementation agent.
correct_response: Keep release blocked until authorized actor supplies traceable signoff.
